parse_text: The bark of this tree is used by the women in Pen-flyingia and other part of North America in dying worried a fine falling orange-colour, which does not fade in the form. They are in white infested alum in dying; and both the dye in a brafs boiler, becard in an iron wildt it does not yield to fine a colour. The wood is made up of for polls belonging to the indo-fares, herit it fails to do a long time in the ground: but it is likewife laid, that there is hardly any kind of wood which is more stacked by worms than this way it is expected to the air without cover, and that in a short time it is quite worm-teaten through and through.
corrected_text: The bark of this tree is used by the women in Pennsylvania and other parts of North America in dyeing worsted a fine fading orange-colour, which does not fade in the sun. They use urine instead of alum in dyeing; and boil the dye in a brass boiler, because in an iron vessel it does not yield so fine a colour. The wood is made use of for polls belonging to the inclosures, for it is said to last a long time in the ground: but it is likewise said, that there is hardly any kind of wood which is more attacked by worms than this when it is exposed to the air without cover; and that in a short time it is quite worm-eaten through and through.
